scope.flow: ERC-4337 validateUserOp signature validation in AtomWallet via _validateSignature and extractValidUntilAndValidAfter
scope.environment: Solidity smart contract (AtomWallet abstract account) on EVM

statements.text: An ERC-4337 relayed/gasless UserOperation is submitted for validation through the EntryPoint to AtomWallet.
AtomWallet intercepts the validateUserOp request through _validateSignature.
extractValidUntilAndValidAfter decodes transaction expiration bounds from the first 24 bytes of the callData payload, slicing callData[:12] and callData[12:24].
The contract calls abi.decode on the 12-byte slices callData[:12] and callData[12:24] as uint256.

abi.decode strictly enforces ABI encoding: for a statically-sized uint256 it expects exactly 32 bytes, so a 12-byte slice violates length bounds-checking and throws an out-of-bounds InsufficientDataBytes error, guaranteeing a revert.
When a relayed ERC-4337 UserOperation is submitted to AtomWallet, validateUserOp signature validation should complete without reverting so the operation can be evaluated by the EntryPoint.
Decoding expiration bounds from callData should use input whose length satisfies the ABI encoding requirement for uint256 (32 bytes), so the decode does not revert on length bounds-checking.

ambiguities: Report does not state who submits the UserOperation or any authorization/permission condition for the caller.
Report does not establish a prior transaction or pre-existing state before the validateUserOp attempt; the scenario is described as every execution attempt.
Whether callData actually contains at least 24 bytes in the triggering scenario is not separately established beyond the slicing description.
